featured_videos.title: 93% Buy Meat At Costco Wrong (Buy This Instead!)
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: 93% Buy Meat At Costco Wrong (Buy This Instead!)
featured_videos.commentary: People are getting *really* specific about Costco cuts in the comments, and honestly, that's the energy we need. One person nailed it mentioning that the line between high Choice and low Prime ribeye is basically invisible to most shoppers, which means you're probably overpaying for Prime when Choice with good marbling does the job just fine. But here's what got me: nobody's talking about the lamb, and based on the comments, that's wild because grass-fed lamb at Costco is apparently a steal that most carnivores are sleeping on. The real takeaway isn't about finding the perfect cut. it's about learning what to actually look for so you're not just grabbing whatever's in front of you, and this video does that work for you.

If you're still experimenting with meal timing or macro ratios, check out our guide on digestion to see if what Max is doing aligns with what might work for you.

featured_videos.title: The Hard Truth About Your First 7 Days on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Hard Truth About Your First 7 Days on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here are basically a masterclass in what actually works. You've got people sharing real numbers. 64 pounds down, metabolic whiplash from a funeral luncheon, the grumpiness that disappears by day five. and it's so much more useful than some influencer's perfect before-and-after. What strikes me most is how many people mention finding the right community and ditching the gatekeepers. Nobody's saying carnivore is magic; they're saying it works *when you're honest about the adjustment and don't pretend day one is the same as day thirty*. One comment nails it: strict means strict at the start, because cheating during adaptation is brutal. Another person mentions undershooting on salt and not realizing it mattered. that's exactly why our electrolytes and salt guide exists, because those details feel boring until your body screams for them. The real takeaway from this thread is that success isn't about finding the "right" version of carnivore or the best YouTube personality; it's about commitment during that rocky first week and surrounding yourself with people who get it.

featured_videos.editorial_title: 3 Years Carnivore- MY Biggest Regret & ASK ME ANYTHING LIVESTREAM
featured_videos.commentary: Three years in and HomeSteadHow's biggest regret isn't what most people expect, which is exactly why this livestream matters. The comments tell the real story, though, especially the person who lost 120 pounds, fell off, gained 60 back, and had to climb out of that hole again. That's the messy part nobody talks about in the highlight reel, and it's the part that actually teaches you something. The fact that people at 70 are finding this and saying "better late than never" shows this isn't about perfection, it's about direction. If you've been thinking about carnivore for years but waiting for the perfect moment, this one's a reality check.

featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Hampton nails what most beginners actually need to hear: stop obsessing over macro calculators and just eat real food. The comments here show exactly why this matters. people are overwhelmed, confused, and ready to try something that works without turning their kitchen into a chemistry lab. The "keep it simple" message is gold, especially that reminder that portion size still counts on keto. If you're starting out and the whole macro tracking thing feels like too much, this plate method approach beats drowning in spreadsheets every time.
